newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close stronger, helped by U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close stronger, helped by U.S. data.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger in moderate trade on Thursday, with tame U.S. inflation and industrial production data helping send prices higher, analysts said.

"The U.S. data was the prime catalyst. There's no surprise there. We had industrial production considerably weaker than what the market was looking for," said Mark Chandler, senior economist with Goldman Sachs Canada. "Canada followed along for the most part."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond closed up C$0.55 to C$119.55 to yield 6.505 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 27/32 to yield 6.56 percent. The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to six basis points from seven basis points at Wednesday's close.

Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets were slightly stronger after the U.S. Labor Department reported that the consumer price index rose 0.2 percent in July, in line with market expectations. A report that industrial production rose 0.2 percent in July and that capacity utilization was 83.1 percent was also seen as positive.
"It just serves to strengthen the story of no imminent (U.S.) rate hike," said Chandler.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.17 to C$109.49 to yield 5.954 percent.
The U.S. 10-year bond rose 18/32 to yield 6.27 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 32 basis points from 37 basis points at Wednesday's close.
The 10-year Canadian government bond futures contract trading on the Montreal Exchange closed up 0.57 to 120.14 with 3909 contracts changing hands.
